item.title: PSG star hailed as ‘most underrated player of all time’ after Barcelona win
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian Ruiz has been hailed as the “most underrated player of all time” after scoring in the Champions League holders’ statement 4-2 victory over Barcelona . Ruiz tapped home PSG’s fourth after the French giants were pegged back twice in their win at the Parc des Princes , first by Xavi Esparti before Lamine Yamal produced his latest moment of magic to level in the 79th minute. Vitinha’s strike two minutes later gave PSG the lead once again and it didn’t take much longer for Ruiz to put the game out of sight, finishing Achraf Hakimi ’s cross. “He could be the most underrated player of all time, Fabian Ruiz,” said Joe Cole on TNT Sports . “He’s won everything in the game, Champions League, does his job, and what I would say is they look a stronger side with him in.” Fabian Ruiz scored PSG's fourth goal (AP) Ruiz came into the season off the back of winning the World Cup with Spain, being an integral figure in midfield alongside Rodri . PSG winger Desire Doue, who brilliantly fired in the opener in Paris, was delighted with his side’s performance. “The atmosphere was crazy tonight,” he said. “We did a great job because we won obviously but we’re really happy with the content of the match. “We did some amazing things, we never quit and when you win against one of the biggest teams in Europe you are really happy so we are really happy tonight. I’m always happy when I can help the team. “Every game you say that we send a message, I don’t know. We just try and play the best football we can and we did a great job tonight.” PSG return to action this weekend against Ligue 1 leaders Lyon, who are above them in the table on goal difference.

item.title: How Pistons' 22-point comeback vs. Celtics made NBA history
item.description: How Pistons' 22-point comeback vs. Celtics made NBA history originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2025-26 NBA season ended with a pair of comebacks from the Knicks , including a historic 29-point turnaround in Game 4 of the NBA Finals. The Pistons didn't quite need to do that to win their season-opener against the Celtics , but they did make some history of their own. Detroit rallied from a 22-point deficit at home to pull off a 121-113 win, at one point unleashing a dominant 23-0 run to turn a game the Celtics once controlled into a comfortable Pistons win. Here's a look at why the Pistons' comeback is unprecedented. Pistons make NBA history with 22-point comeback The Pistons pulled off the largest comeback on the first day of an NBA season since 1997-98, when detailed in-game records were first kept. Not only did the Pistons manage to rally from a 22-point deficit on the opening day of the season, but they did so in the very first game of the season for any team and were facing a team with championship hopes. The Pistons’ 22-point comeback is the largest comeback on the first day of an NBA season in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98). https://t.co/qICSxEp998 — NBA Communications (@NBAPR) October 20, 2026 The Pistons trailed 72-50 at one point in the third quarter, getting bludgeoned by Paul George's hot shooting in his Celtics debut. While George finished with 38 points on 12-of-21 shooting, Jayson Tatum shot just 6-of-23 in a nightmarish performance. Duncan Robinson, meanwhile, supported Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren with 21 points on five 3-pointers. J.B. Bickerstaff undoubtedly will want some better starts from his team, but the win put the Pistons on the board with a win ahead of a matchup with Giannis Antetokounmpo and the new-look Heat on Friday. item.title: "We showed character" – Hoeneß and Führich proud of Stuttgart's efforts against Atlético Madrid
item.description: "We showed character" – Hoeneß and Führich proud of Stuttgart's efforts against Atlético Madrid Sebastian Hoeneß displayed mixed emotions as he digested VfB Stuttgart's performance after their 1-1 draw with Atlético Madrid tonight. “I am proud of the performance of the team. Our first half was incredible,” Hoeneß said in the mixed zone with UEFA.tv at full-time. “We showed character, and to be honest, a two-goal lead would have been possible with the [first-half] chances we made,” he added. “The goal [we conceded] after 90 seconds in the second half was too fast, then the game looked a bit more open. “After the red card it was a game on, one goal, and we had some chances to win, that's why there is some disappointment," he summarized. Man of the match Chris Führich echoed his coach, claiming he was “more proud of the performance than disappointed over the result.” "We played a really good game from the beginning, and now we can take some of the positives and look forward now. “I think we deserve more, we were the better team and had more chances. In the end it feels like we lost two points,” Führich added.

item.title: Ferrari development driver reveals confirmed F1 test plans
item.description: Motorsport photo After joining Ferrari as a simulator and development driver this summer, Sacha Fenestraz has said that the Italian team has promised him a Formula 1 test in 2027. This comes after the driver moved from Mercedes' Brackley headquarters to Ferrari's in Maranello. Speaking to Grande Premio during the Fuji race weekend for Super Formula, he confirmed his drive next year. “The truth is, it’s a dream to be able to work there, and it’s a dream to be with such a big name in motorsport," he said. "The work is great; it’s a bit like what I did with Mercedes in Brackley, only now I get to eat some good pasta in Italy and drive a Formula 1 Ferrari in the simulator, and potentially a couple of tests next year as well, so it’s a really great opportunity. “I’m going to have a test next year, I already know that and they confirmed it. I was supposed to be there next week, but I can’t make it because I have the Super GT race at Autopolis, so oh well, it’ll happen eventually." The Scuderia team is yet to confirm it, while the Argentine has said the purpose of it is to make him a better simulator driver. Sacha Fenestraz, VANTELIN TEAM TOM’S Sacha Fenestraz, VANTELIN TEAM TOM’S "I’m really looking forward to it, but obviously the most important thing for them is for me to get in the car to improve my simulator performance. All the simulator drivers have to get behind the wheel of a TPC car to gain experience in a Formula 1 car, so I’ll just have to wait for that day." Fenestraz has had a successful racing career so far in Japan, winning the 2019 All-Japan Formula 3 championship and racing in Super Formula and Super GT. He also spent time in Formula E with Nissan. He finished 16th in both the 2022 and 2023 championships. At Ferrari, Dino Beganovic will become reserve driver in 2027, alongside Antonio Giovinazzi , after leaving the team's Driver Academy. item.title: Urban Meyer only has one concern about a 24-team College Football Playoff
item.description: Credit: The Herd, FS1 Urban Meyer won three national titles as a college football head coach, but the game is already very different from his time at Florida and Ohio State. The ways NIL and the transfer portal have shifted the sport’s landscape were hard to predict, and the Fox Sports college football analyst is among those who misread how they’ve changed it. “I misfired on the whole conversation about NIL and transfer portal,” Meyer said during an appearance on The Herd with Colin Cowherd. “I thought the rich would get richer. What it’s done is make parity in college football.” “I misfired on the whole conversation about NIL and transfer portal. I thought the rich would get richer. What it’s done is make parity in college football.” – Urban Meyer https://t.co/URKSjxckXE — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 19, 2026 Parity is perhaps a bit strong. Yes, Indiana transformed from a basement-dweller to national champion in two years. But for the most part, the same traditional powerhouse programs are still at the top of the heap. Things are a little more crowded, and “second-tier programs” like Texas Tech, SMU, and UCLA have a chance to rise quickly. But at the end of the day, we’re still mostly talking about the same Big Ten, SEC, Big 12, and ACC schools dominating the landscape. Another aspect of the game that’s rapidly changing from Meyer’s day is the expanding College Football Playoff. When he led Ohio State to a national title in 2015, the CFP included four teams. By all accounts, it will have 24 teams starting next season . Meyer doesn’t sound too opposed to the decision , though he does have one concern about what the program could lose. “At first I couldn’t stand the idea,” Meyer said on The Triple Option. “ I just thought you would dilute the product, but what I’m witnessing this year and we’re all learning is that the parity is unbelievable. “The only concern I have, and I’ll keep saying this as long as I’m around, those who say that conference championship games are not important, I will say never played in it, never coached in it, and never won a ring. I think conference championship games are one of the most exciting things that have ever happened in my lifetime and certainly for my players.” To make room for the expanded first round, conference championship games will likely go away, which changes the calculus in ways beyond just being able to say you won . And as much as college football has changed since Meyer last coached there, the ripple effects of the latest seismic shift are only just beginning to be felt. item.title: “Still underestimated” Jonathan Tah says Arsenal man is not appreciated enough
item.description: “Still underestimated” Jonathan Tah says Arsenal man is not appreciated enough Jonathan Tah and Kai Havertz spent a long time together at Bayer Leverkusen and built a strong friendship that goes beyond the pitch before they both left the club. Havertz first left for England, where he played for Chelsea before moving to Arsenal, while Tah moved to Bayern Munich last season, and both players will meet this week. Arsenal faces Bayern in their next Champions League game, and it will be an interesting match between two of the favourites to win the Champions League this season. The Gunners will want to win that match, but it would be easier said than done as they will be facing some of the best players on the planet. Tah’s Praise for Havertz Bayern also know that Arsenal would be a tough nut to crack, and it could be a thriller, even though Arsenal’s defensive style does not allow them to play adventurously, and it will be interesting to see how the Gunners’ attack will perform. However, Tah thinks Havertz is certainly still being underestimated around the world. He said, as quoted by Bavarian Football Works : “Kai is my friend of ten years. Great character, amazing player, a player who is still underestimated, to be fair. I don’t think he gets the appreciation he deserves. We already talked about the game. I’m really looking forward to it.” (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) A Clash Between Two European Giants Tah’s comments highlight the respect between the two players, and their reunion will add a personal edge to the fixture. Havertz’s quality has often been overlooked, but his role at Arsenal has been important. The German’s versatility and intelligence make him a key figure. The match itself promises to be a fascinating tactical battle, with both sides among the favourites for the competition. Arsenal’s defensive organisation will be tested by Bayern’s attacking talent, and the Gunners will need to be at their best. Bayern’s strength is well known, but Arsenal’s home advantage and recent form give them confidence. The encounter will be a measure of their European credentials. Havertz’s performance could be decisive, and Tah will be keen to get one over his old friend. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson sends strong message to Karl-Anthony Towns about contract extension
item.description: Knicks' Jalen Brunson sends strong message to Karl-Anthony Towns about contract extension originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks are going to be heavily watched this season, not just because they are the defending champions, but also because of what is happening internally. Players eligible for contract extensions had discussions before the season began, but negotiations can be risky at times. The two main players involved in the discussions were Josh Hart and Karl-Anthony Towns. Both are major staples of the Knicks' roster. However, New York decided to pause all negotiations to focus on the regular season. “As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of. As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season," a Knicks spokesperson told ESPN's Shams Charania. Towns has been the more vocal of the two about his displeasure with how things unfolded. Knicks superstar and Finals MVP Jalen Brunson let the media know how Towns and Hart would handle the situation. “He's going to be professional. Not just him - everybody. Everyone's going to be professional and continue to do their jobs," Brunson said. Towns knows he is going to have to take a pay cut, but he isn't going to accept a massive one. The veteran has been vocal about wanting to stay with the Knicks if he can get a contract that reflects his value. On Tuesday, in an interview with ESPN’s Malika Andrews, Brunson made it clear what he wants Towns to do. “Sign the contract,” Brunson told Andrews. It is clear that Brunson wants Towns to stay, and so does the rest of the team. Towns is a well-respected player around the league, but he isn't going to settle for a contract worth significantly less than his value. Brunson has sent a clear message that he wants a deal done, so it is now up to the organization to work things out with Towns. This Knicks roster is very connected, so there is little reason for the team to break up its core. item.title: Yaya Toure admits defeat: “The gap with Roma is too big.”
item.description: Yaya Toure admits defeat: “The gap with Roma is too big.” Roma were superior throughout the entire 90 minutes at the Olimpico against Slovan Bratislava. The Giallorossi won 4-0, and the Slovakians never seemed capable of getting back into the game. Yaya Touré, the visiting coach, spoke about the match in the capital at a press conference. The initial approach? “We had prepared very well, it was disappointing because we could have done better, but instead we were passive. On pitches like this, you pay for it, and then it becomes complicated. We paid for our mistakes, we must improve, otherwise it will be tough for the rest of the tournament.” “I think they’re working very well defensively, they make very few mistakes. My players have to enjoy themselves when they’re on the pitch; football is about having fun, being together. We’re not united. There are some positive things, but we’re not focused for 90 minutes, and that’s disappointing. We’ve worked on it, but there’s a lot to do. We have to fight and help each other. There’s a lot to learn from a Roma like this; I know how we need to improve, and we’ll try to do so.” “If we compare ourselves to Roma, they have millions to spend. A successful rebuild like the Jazz just pulled off can create its own financial complications. When a team struggles, it often has inexpensive young players and plenty of room to experiment. When those players improve, their next contracts can make it harder to retain everyone while continuing to add talent. item.title: Iraola delighted with Liverpool youngster’s development after starring in comeback win
item.description: Iraola delighted with Liverpool youngster’s development after starring in comeback win Andoni Iraola praised Rio Ngumoha’s growing influence after the 18-year-old impressed in Liverpool’s win over Villarreal. The winger set up Liverpool’s second and third goals on the night as they came from 2-0 down to win 4-3 at Anfield . “I think he was coming from a very good second half against Brentford,” Iraola said. “Today he didn’t have an easy game because they were demanding him defensively but offensively he’s very difficult to stop. “If we can put him in situations one v one where he can get into the box, normally he makes plays, he produces things. “The assist for Alexis is lovely play. He can even go down for a penalty but decides to continue and makes a great decision.” The Liverpool boss also highlighted Ngumoha’s improving fitness and willingness to learn. “Endurance wise, he’s been able to play more minutes,” Iraola said. “We were pushing him a little bit, he was tired but he’s done a good effort and really happy for him. “I’m happy with his attitude because he wants to improve the things we think he needs to improve.” Ngumoha has also been asked to operate from different positions, something Iraola believes is helping to develop his game further. “He’s eager to add more things to his game, has changed sides a lot,” he said. “He’s played on the right a lot recently and is feeling so comfortable now, adding some shots with the left foot. “If he can add these small things to his game it will put him in an even better position and that’s the good thing with Rio.” But Iraola also urged patience with the teenager. “He’s still 18, he can still add things and I hope he continues in the same way. “It’s not always going to be like this, he will have ups and downs in the process.”

item.title: Aston Martin announces first-of-its-kind F1 partnership ahead of US GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Aston Martin has become the first Formula 1 team to partner with a padel and pickleball company, teaming up with Padeltek for a range of rackets that will go on sale this week. The Silverstone outfit announced the new collaboration ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, where the team and Padeltek will host an exclusive I / AM fan event at a brand-new padel venue, Padel Society. The Aston Martin Padeltek collection will include three padel rackets and three cover bags. "Formula 1 is a platform for collaboration across wider sport and lifestyle spaces, and we're continuing to see the growing demand from fans to bring the worlds together," Aston Martin head of licensing and merchandise Matt Chapman explained. "As the first Formula 1 team to formally partner with a padel and pickleball company, we're excited to combine our brand DNA via a tangible product that feels authentic and performance-driven." Taking to the padel court. Aston Martin Aramco collaborate with Padeltek, bringing the world of Formula One and padel together. Find out more here: https://t.co/4lSWJanKlB https://t.co/f9kCZ3veMI — Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team (@AstonMartinF1) October 19, 2026 Ron Saslow, founding and managing partner of Thirty-5 Capital, added: "It didn't take long for padel and Formula 1 to find each other. Both sports reward precision, speed and performance, and both are attracting a growing fan base here in the United States. "For Padeltek, collaborating with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team is an opportunity to bring that shared energy to the court, creating equipment that gives racing fans a new way to connect with their team while introducing more people to padel." The partnership will continue to expand in 2027, with pickleball rackets and accessories planned for release. Padel has become increasingly popular among F1 drivers, with many now incorporating it into their training routines. Aston Martin heads into the United States Grand Prix, which is scheduled for 23-25 October, 10th in the constructors' standings with seven points. Two-time champion Fernando Alonso is 17th in the drivers' championship, having earned all seven of the team's points, and his team-mate Lance Stroll is 21st with no points. item.title: Manchester City 5 AEK Athens 1: City player ratings as Phil Foden stars at the Etihad
item.description: Manchester City 5 AEK Athens 1: City player ratings as Phil Foden stars at the Etihad Manchester City 5 (Elliot Anderson 12′, Phil Foden 34′, 65′, 76′, Rayan Cherki 57′) AEK Athens 1 (Stavros Pilios 52′) Here are the City player ratings as Manchester City beat AEK Athens 5-1 to make it two wins out of three in the UEFA Champions League league phase. Phil Foden scored a hat trick and goals from Rayan Cherki and Elliot Anderson sealed City’s win. Enzo Maresca’s side were given a scare when Stavros Pilios made it 2-1 in the 52nd minute. From that point onwards, City put their foot down to come away with the three points they needed after their defeat to PSG last week. City player ratings. Gianluigi Donnarumma-6/10: Rarely called upon in goal and some of his passing was good, and on other occasions not so. Rico Lewis-8.5/10: These are the games that suit Rico Lewis. He picked up two assists and he worked tirelessly on City’s right-hand side. Abdukodir Khusanov- 7.5/10: Khusanov looked much more comfortable at centre-back. His recovery pace and strength helped quell the threat of AEK Athens on multiple occasions. Ruben Dias- 6.5/10: Manchester City’s captain did what he had to do tonight, nothing more. Josko Gvardiol-7/10: As usual Gvardiol offered a threat going forward. Hopefully the knock he received isn’t too serious. Elliot Anderson-8/10: Anderson scored his first City goal and he was good both in and out of possession. Enzo Fernandez-7/10: Another good display from Enzo Fernandez without being spectacular. Allan-7.5/10: I really liked Allan’s game on the left wing. He made several dangerous runs and he looks to be a real weapon with the ball at his feet. A promising display from him. Rayan Cherki-8.5/10: I thought Cherki was untidy early before he grew into the game. Some of his tricks and flicks were sublime as was his goal. Phil Foden-10/10: An absolutely brilliant performance from Foden. His hat trick capped off his night and his touch and confidence looks to be back. Floyd Samba- 7/10: Samba was lively throughout and it was his run which set up the free kick for Elliot Anderson’s goal. I liked his work out of possession hence the 7/10 for his display. Substitutes Ryan McAidoo-7/10: McAidoo was lively after coming on and grabbed an assist for his efforts. Rayan Ait-Nouri-6/10: Ait-Nouri came on late with the game won and had some nice touches. Vitor Reis-6/10: He was involved in the build up to Foden’s third goal and he is a player I want to see play more often. Kaden Braithwaite-6/10: It was good to him get on the pitch late on.

item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Kurt Warner pinpoints 1 major flaw leading to Rams’ struggles appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford is on the verge of setting a record he wants no part of, the Rams are trying to find a kicker once again. Through it all, Kurt Warner pinpointed one major flaw leading to the Rams’ struggles, according to a post on X by the Rich Eisen Show. “You’re looking for things that can close out games,” Warner said. “Yes, they can throw the football. And yes, they’ve got good weapons on the outside. And a reigning MVP at quarterback. But what made them so good in the past, and even last year, was their ability to run the football. Especially when you get down in the red zone, to finish drives by running the football. And having that physicality up front. I don’t see that right now.” Rams searching for answers after 2-4 start Of course, McVay is taking the brunt of criticism for letting this loaded team go off the rails early in the season. McVay tried to own it , according to Fox Sports. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I have to do a better job and figure out how exactly we settle guys down,” McVay said following Sunday’s shocking loss to the Cardinals. “But we’ve had some really critical errors at some really unfortunate times. That’s what our narrative has been this year. And we can’t keep saying that we haven’t done that before, because this year we are doing it. We have to be able to fix it. And it’s my job to do that.” Running back Blake Corum said the Rams are experiencing a reality check. “But we know that we’re good,” Corum said. “We know we have the guys. We know we have the culture. We know we have the team. But, like Coach [McVay] said, it’s time to get back to work. We have to watch this film and see where things aren’t aligning and then fix those things.” The other running back, Kyren Williams, said the Rams need to simply deal with the issues and move forward. “You use this adversity for moments in the future that’s going to allow us to be who we want to be,” Williams said. item.title: How Gattuso Outwitted Spalletti in Juventus vs Lazio Showdown
item.description: How Gattuso Outwitted Spalletti in Juventus vs Lazio Showdown On Sunday, Lazio outplayed Juventus en route to a historic 3-0 win, as Gennaro Gattuso got the better of Luciano Spalletti from a tactical standpoint. The Background The two managers had crossed paths on several occasions in the past, including Derby della Madonnina clashes between Gattuso’s AC Milan and Spalletti’s Inter. Moreover, both of them took their current roles in the hopes of rebounding from a miserable tenure at the helm of the Italian national team. But while the Calabrian is finding joy in his early days in Rome, the Tuscan is struggling in Turin. Lazio Stunned Juventus On Their Own Ground Ahead of Sunday’s meeting, Lazio were surprisingly five points ahead of the Old Lady. By the end of the evening, the gap was widened to eight points, with the teams’ displays fully justifying it. Player Ratings: Juventus 0-3 Lazio – Oliver the Conqueror While many would argue that Juventus, despite their many absences, boast the better team, Il Corriere dello Sport highlights Gattuso’s tactical tweaks as one of the main reasons behind the large result. Christos Mandas Was at the Centre of Gattuso’s Plot The Roman newspaper noted how the 48-year-old asked Christos Mandas to act as the third defender in the buildup, joining Oliver Provstgaard and Josip Sutalo. The Greek goalkeeper effectively took the role Reda Belahyane had been performing in recent weeks. The Moroccan instead operated in a slightly higher position. Moreover, Gattuso sent his box-to-box midfielders, Kenneth Taylor and Davide Frattesi, further forward to form a five-man attacking unit alongside Tijjani Noslin, Mattia Zaccagni and Gustav Isaksen. Lazio Have Found the Perfect Successors for Romagnoli & Gila – Opinion The idea was to lure in the Juventus attacker and invite them to press high, before sending the ball forward through Mandas. While the goalkeeper’s long passes weren’t always on cue, Lazio had enough men forward to pounce on second balls and cause havoc in the opposition’s area. Lazio Outran Juventus In addition to this tactical manoeuvre, Gattuso encouraged his players to engage in one-on-one duels. His gruelling pre-season training is also paying off, with the Biancocelesti outrunning Spalletti’s men 122,894 km to 117,035 km.

item.title: OU basketball's Duke Brennan granted preliminary injunction for season, per reports
item.description: NORMAN — Oklahoma men's basketball center Duke Brennan received positive news concerning his eligibility status Tuesday. A California judge granted a preliminary injunction that gives Brennan and others named in the Glancey v. NCAA case eligibility through the end of the upcoming season, according to multiple reports . The lawsuit involves 76 basketball players, mostly from the 2022 recruiting class, who previously received a temporary restraining order. Following Tuesday's ruling, Brennan remains eligible to play for the Sooners. The NCAA is expected to appeal, according to multiple reports. More: Retaining OU basketball PG Xzayvier Brown crucial to Sooners' plan under Porter Moser Brennan, a fifth-year transfer portal big, is coming off a career year at Villanova where he averaged a double-double and earned All-Big East honors. He averaged 12.4 points and 10.3 rebounds per game, while recording 14 double-doubles and helping lead the Wildcats to the NCAA Tournament. While Brennan is currently eligible, fifth-year guard B.J. Edwards , who transferred to OU from SMU, is currently ineligible after the Tennessee Court of Appeals issued an order on Aug. 26 staying the injunction granted to plaintiff athletes in that case, pending appeal. "The hardest thing for all of us is the uncertainty," Sooners coach Porter Moser said in an interview with CBS Sports last week. OU opens its season against East Texas A&M at 7 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 2 at Lloyd Noble Center. Colton Sulley covers the Oklahoma Sooners for The Oklahoman. Have a story idea for Colton? He can be reached at csulley@oklahoman.com or on X/Twitter at @colton_sulley. The Blue Hens’ challenge this week is Missouri State, which also moved up from the FCS last year and joined Delaware in Conference USA, making this the first football meeting between the schools. The Blue Hens are expected to have Nick Minicucci back at quarterback after he has missed the last 2 1/2 games with a knee injury. Minicucci, his right knee braced, was in uniform and taking first-team snaps in the pregame, which he had not the last two games. Inside linebacker Colin Gallagher, Delaware's second-leading tackler, is sidelined, however. Missouri State moved to CUSA from the powerful Missouri Valley Football Conference, in which it was not one of the league kingpins. The Bears made the Division I-AA/FCS playoffs just four times from 1982-2024, winning only their first postseason game in 1989. Delaware was a far more consistent playoff qualifier, despite an unprecedented and agonizing drought from 2011-17 and made the postseason its last two FCS seasons in 2022 and 2023. “Watching them in crossover tape, they were a talented football team last year and it was good to see that,” Carty said of Missouri State. Missouri State went 5-3 in CUSA last year and 7-6 overall, losing in the Xbox Bowl to Arkansas State. Delaware won the 68 Ventures Bowl to also go 7-6 but was 4-4 in league games. The Bears are under first-year coach Casey Woods, the former SMU offensive coordinator, after previous coach Ryan Beard got the Coastal Carolina job. item.title: Boston Celtics fall to Detroit Pistons 121-113 with familiar late collapse (PHOTOS)
item.description: The Boston Celtics started their 2026-27 NBA regular season off on the wrong foot after falling to the Detroit Pistons 121-113 despite building a 22-point lead early, collapsing in familiar form in the game's final frame. Unlike their undefeated preseason slate of games, Boston lost the battle of the boards 49-39 despite shooting better from 3 (40 percent to 38), taking 2 more shot attempts, and making 3 more steals. The Celtics were outscored in the paint 44-34, and in transition (11-14) as well, leading to an ending all too familiar to fans of the team that saw early efficiency crumble in the face of a stout comeback from the Pistons. With the loss, the Celtics fall to 0-1 to start their current campaign, and won't be able to have a shot at getting back to .500 until they take on the reigning champion New York Knicks on Friday (Oct. 23) night. Let's take a look at all of the best plays captured in images from the loss. Listen to "A look at the Pritchard extension, Boston Celtics preseason play, and more" on Spreaker. (Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images) | Getty Images “Cobe” is back. Top Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Welterweight prospect Jacobe Smith will step in on 12 days’ notice to face veteran Randy Brown in the UFC Vegas 123 co-main event next weekend (Sat., Oct. 31, 2026) inside Meta Apex in Las Vegas, Nevada. Heavy.com was first to report the news. Brown was originally scheduled to face Carlos Leal , but Leal was forced to withdraw from the Halloween showdown. Smith (13-0) has yet to receive a full training camp for any of his four UFC appearances. That hasn’t stopped the undefeated 30-year-old from absolutely demolishing his opposition . “Cobe” is coming off a first-round knockout win over Bruce Whitehead at UFC 332, needing less than two minutes to dispatch the short-notice newcomer ( watch highlights ). Before that, Smith nuked Josiah Harrell in three minutes at UFC Houston earlier this year ( watch highlights ). Smith will now attempt to finish 2026 with a perfect 3-0 record while picking up the biggest win of his young career. Brown (20-8), meanwhile, badly needs a victory when he enters the Octagon on Halloween. “Rudeboy” is riding a two-fight losing streak, falling to Gabriel Bonfim ( watch highlights ) in his first UFC main event before most recently losing to Kevin Holland — the same man Smith has repeatedly called out . Brown is 4-3 across his last seven UFC appearances and represents a considerable step up in experience for the unbeaten prospect. However, accepting dangerous fights without a full camp has quickly become Smith’s specialty. item.description: Not just Ngumoha: Liverpool star who won 7 duels was ‘excellent’ against Villarreal Rio Ngumoha was the undoubted star of the show for Liverpool in their 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday night, but he wasn’t alone in delivering a magnificent individual performance for the Reds. item.title: Lawson climbs above F1's biggest names after yet another strong showing
item.description: Liam Lawson has continued to impress in the 2026 Formula 1 season, with his performance at the Singapore Grand Prix earning him second place in the weekend's Power Rankings and lifting him to fourth in the overall standings. The Power Rankings are compiled by five judges who assess each driver's performance over the weekend, taking into account their individual contribution rather than simply their finishing position or the capabilities of their car. The Racing Bulls driver enjoyed another competitive outing at Marina Bay, delivering strong performances across both qualifying sessions and the two races. His efforts did not go unnoticed by Formula 1's judging panel, which ranked him among the weekend's leading performers. Only Max Verstappen received a higher rating in Singapore, with Lawson finishing ahead of several drivers competing in considerably more competitive machinery. Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Lawson moves ahead of Norris and Russell in F1 season rankings The Singapore result has strengthened Lawson's standing across the entire campaign. With 17 rounds completed, the New Zealander has risen two positions to fourth in the season-long Power Rankings, recording an average rating of 7.6 out of 10. Kimi Antonelli remains comfortably ahead of the field with an average of 8.7, followed by Verstappen on 8.2 and Lewis Hamilton on 7.7. Lawson is now the highest-ranked Racing Bulls driver and sits above several established names. George Russell, Pierre Gasly and reigning world champion Lando Norris share fifth place on 7.5, while teammate Arvid Lindblad occupies eighth with a 7.4 average. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Isack Hadjar are further behind, both averaging 7.2 and sharing ninth position. Lawson's rise is particularly notable given that Racing Bulls have spent much of the campaign fighting in the midfield. His position reflects the impression he has made on the judging panel throughout the year rather than the number of championship points he has collected. Lawson opens door to surprise racing opportunity in 2027 Away from Formula 1, Lawson has also set his sights on another major motorsport event, having recently expressed interest in taking part in the 2027 Race of Champions. The competition is set to take place in Wellington, New Zealand, with former Formula 1 drivers Sebastian Vettel and Valtteri Bottas among the confirmed participants. For Lawson, the prospect of competing on home soil against some of the sport's biggest names is particularly appealing. Lawson recently welcomed the possibility of joining the event, although his participation has yet to be confirmed. It would offer the New Zealander a rare opportunity to race in front of his home crowd, with Formula 1 currently having no Grand Prix in the country.

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
